hook.title: A shared paint palette
hook.text: Instead of mixing every relation's colour from scratch, give *all* relations one shared **palette** of $B$ basis colours $V_1,\dots,V_B$. Each relation then only records its own **recipe**: how much of each palette colour to mix, $a_{r1},\dots,a_{rB}$. If the palette has a handful of colours but there are hundreds of relations, you save enormously. If every relation gets its own palette colour ($B\approx|R|$), you've saved nothing.
hook.recall: Remember the shared palette: $W_r=\sum_ba_{rb}V_b$ with bases shared by all relations; huge savings when $B\ll|R|$, none when $B\approx|R|$.

tasks: Keep $|R|=100$. Increase $B$ from 1 to 50. When do the savings disappear?
With $B\ll|R|$ what is the saving factor?
explore.takeaway: $W_r=\sum_{b=1}^Ba_{rb}V_b$; parameters per layer: $(d^{(l+1)}\times d^{(l)}+|R|)\times B$ instead of $d^{(l+1)}\times d^{(l)}\times|R|$. Basis matrices are per layer and learned with backprop.

build.template: $W_r=\sum_{b=1}^{B}$ {0} $V_b$, where the $V_b$ are {1} across relations and the {2} are specific to relation $r$.
build.explanation: Slide 29: represent each relation’s matrix as a linear combination of basis transformations; $\{V_b\}$ are shared; $a_{rb}$ are the importance weights for relation $r$ and basis $V_b$.

questions.prompt: $d^{(l+1)}=d^{(l)}=64$, $|R|=100$ relations, $B=5$ bases. Parameters per layer with basis learning $(d^{(l+1)}d^{(l)}+|R|)\cdot B$?
questions.explanation: $(4096+100)\cdot5=20{,}980$, compared with $4096\cdot100=409{,}600$ for the full model.

questions.prompt: When does basis learning give significant savings?
In basis learning which quantities are shared across relations?
questions.explanation: Each relation owns only its coefficients.

options: Basis matrices and coefficients are all learnable by backpropagation
Typically each layer has its own set of basis matrices
Bases are usually shared across layers
questions.explanation: “Typically, basis matrices are not shared across layers.”
Each relation mixes the shared bases with its own coefficients.

questions.prompt: *“With $B=|R|$ bases we get the best regularisation, since every relation has its own basis.”* What’s wrong?
options: With $B\approx|R|$ the parameter savings diminish; basis learning helps when $B\ll|R|$
questions.explanation: A palette with one colour per relation saves nothing.
